records.reason: m186 under pure EA at 150 uL tests loading transfer of the exceptional 31.65/31.72 mL low-loading observation 04ecdea4151183669394. Its ordinary low-loading 1/1 result, 47328994eb7953d68919, makes another pure-EA loading valuable for distinguishing a condition-specific pattern from isolated recorded variability.

m186 at 1/1 and 100 uL checks whether the updated model spreads its pure-EA anomaly into an adjacent ratio and loading. Compare with measured low-loading 1/1 record 47328994eb7953d68919 and high-loading 2/1 record a352cfd369602fd71eec to constrain that correction locally.

The positional hydroxybenzaldehyde isomer m190 has a predicted pure-EA onset of 20.82 mL, much later than its measured 10/1 onset of 6.22 mL in 2029b30e714e5ff498bf. This tests possible transfer of the unusual m186 boundary label without treating that predicted nonmonotonicity as an observed finding.

Existing 10/1 and 20/1 records 2029b30e714e5ff498bf and d1774335b45258bc173a provide weaker-eluent references, allowing the labels to distinguish a genuine strong-eluent boundary response from inappropriate structural transfer.

Iodophenol at 10/1 and 50 uL fills an intermediate ratio after the large 50/1 miss in 95d1d257dfea69f178f8. Together with the selected low-loading 20/1 point and measured 5/1 anchor 1150272392a90f36db05, it defines a useful fixed-loading response segment.

Iodophenol at 20/1 and 50 uL supplies a loading contrast to b66aa101a244885dd587, measured at 150 uL. The latest same-loading 20/1-to-50/1 growth was much steeper than predicted, so this label tests whether the earlier transition also depends on loading.

Iodophenol under pure EA at 150 uL tests a predicted onset of 10.07 mL against the measured 1/1 onset of 4.82 mL in 3fe8b9db9fbe9d0dedc4. This anchors the strong-eluent boundary while the other selected iodophenol points locate later growth, preventing its weak-eluent failure from inducing a uniform shift.

Methyl mandelate at 5/1 and 50 uL extends the new low-loading 2/1 observation 30456dafbfe681b5af70 toward measured 10/1 record d8fcb58722028dbf9c02. Recent 2/1 predictions missed onset more than completion, making this point useful for locating where endpoint-specific loading differences grow.

Methyl mandelate at 5/1 and 150 uL completes the selected loading contrast, with measured 100 uL record 12ab195583f05b9aa177 as a midpoint. The model predicts nearly identical outputs across these loadings, whereas 10/1 records d8fcb58722028dbf9c02 and 7bbdec21c428010dd67b show a larger onset contrast than completion contrast.

Methyl anthranilate at 50/1 and 100 uL tests the predicted 22.61/46.28 mL extension beyond its measured 20/1 point 10f14f6ee69ba06bbe68. Comparison with ethyl anthranilate's 50/1 record 249b884b29177edb9df5 can teach whether late-ratio growth transfers between these closely related aminoesters.

Methylbenzyl alcohol at 1/1 and 50 uL locates the early part of the low-loading curve before measured 2/1 record 4db6b065867770d9dbd9. It provides a related alcohol comparison after the methoxybenzyl-alcohol failure in 71abc36775b6cce56da7, without assuming the methoxy substituent correction should transfer.

Methylbenzyl alcohol at 10/1 and 50 uL extends measured low-loading 5/1 record a5446977630484ca5fe1. Same-ratio measurements at 100 and 150 uL, 75232f4ee5de52a0499e and d05a91dc8e32e9edd7d0, make this a direct test of loading-associated onset and completion behavior.

Measured low-loading 1/1 record b655d7de0986cbd0d622 and 100 uL 5/1 record 892c3900698d3de38b1c constrain its own curve before sulfur-related endpoint corrections are shared between carbonyl classes.

m3 at 50/1 and 100 uL pairs with its selected 5/1 point and measured 20/1 record c25aed72c162a62800ce. The labels test the predicted intermediate-ratio completion maximum at fixed loading, providing a counterexample or confirmation outside the polar families dominating recent failures.

hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on molecule and PE/EA and can affect onset and completion differently. The latest mandelate measurements support an onset-specific correction, while the much larger methoxybenzyl-alcohol contrast shows that a single small loading offset is insufficient. Recorded associations do not establish a causal loading mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor remains nearly insensitive to loading across many candidate tuples. Matched contrasts and missing loading midpoints can teach endpoint-specific interactions while preserving cases where pooling across loadings is adequate. Unrecorded variability may explain part of the contrasts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the mandelate, aromatic-alcohol, tertiary-alcohol and alpha-ketoester selections show loading differences that change with PE/EA, and are those differences concentrated in V1, V2, or both?

hypotheses.content: PE/EA response curvature and endpoint coupling require scaffold-specific structure–condition relationships. In particular, iodophenol's measured high-loading 20/1-to-50/1 growth rejects the previous predicted flattening. Other ester, ketone and donor-containing families need their own transition locations rather than a uniform polarity correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels in ratio gaps can identify where growth starts, steepens or separates between endpoints. Fixed-loading local curves and comparisons across connectivity can constrain the model without treating cross-molecule differences as controlled causal substitution effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How much response growth occurs at the selected intermediate ratios, and do the predicted local onset or completion maxima survive measurement in phenol, boronate, carbonyl and nonpolar aromatic environments?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent endpoint patterns vary across aromatic aldehydes, and the predictor may overtransfer unusual individual labels between loadings or related structures. The latest late, nearly coincident pure-EA endpoints for m186 do not yet establish a general late-onset hydroxybenzaldehyde response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The current pure-EA predictions for m186 and m190 and the 1/1 completion maximum for methylthiobenzaldehyde are useful tests of how isolated endpoint patterns spread through shared representations. Localizing these patterns could improve many strong-eluent rows without imposing a universal aldehyde shortening or lengthening correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m186 pure-EA pattern recur at higher loading, does m190 show it under a fixed-loading pure-EA/1/1 comparison, and is the sulfur-containing aldehyde's predicted completion maximum real?

hypotheses.content: Large weak-eluent discrepancies in sulfoxide, formally charged P/O and nitrobenzophenone records can coexist with comparatively ordinary strong-eluent baselines. The latest measurements strengthen the case for local condition-dependent corrections rather than a global heteroatom or formal-charge shift.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These confirmed baselines reduce the expected value of spending this batch on more nearby strong-eluent anchors for the same three environments. They also discourage spreading extreme weak-ratio labels across all conditions. Speciation and other possible explanations remain unmeasured.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where feasible, do repeated weak-eluent tuples reproduce the contrasting loading patterns while the strong-eluent baselines remain modest?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes sharpened the emphasis on loading and condition localization. Methyl mandelate at 2/1 measured 11.57/15.78 and 9.89/15.47 mL at 50 and 100 uL: completion forecasts were close, while onset was underestimated. That supports extending its loading comparison at 5/1. Methoxybenzyl alcohol at low-loading 5/1 measured 50.73/71.53 mL against 16.56/25.82 mL predicted, whereas the previously measured 100 uL condition was much shorter. This is a major recorded contrast, but missing factors prevent attributing it solely to loading; it motivates controlled comparisons among the remaining alcohol conditions. Iodophenol at high-loading 50/1 measured 52.83/97.93 mL, rejecting the predicted flattening beyond its 20/1 anchor and motivating intermediate-ratio labels. Conversely, m186 under pure EA produced late, nearly coincident endpoints while its 1/1 result remained ordinary. I therefore test loading and positional-isomer transfer rather than generalizing that record across hydroxybenzaldehydes. The short ortho-methylbenzaldehyde pure-EA completion and broader dimethylbenzaldehyde results continue to weaken any universal aldehyde correction. Accurate or modest-error latest baselines for sulfoxide, P/O and nitrobenzophenone strengthen H4 and lower their priority this round. All cited acquisition errors are historical forecasts, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch combines linked experiments whose labels can distinguish specific explanations. The m186/m190 block tests localization and structural transfer of an exceptional strong-eluent observation. The iodophenol selections connect its newly established steep weak-eluent response to missing earlier ratios and a potentially unusual strong-eluent baseline. Mandelate has a matched 5/1 loading comparison with an existing midpoint; methylbenzyl alcohol, the naphthyl alcohols, m51, phenylpropanol and benzoylformate add loading contrasts or missing curve points where endpoint behavior can change independently. These experiments address the latest failures through relationships that can transfer across related rows, while allowing different directions of association.

The remaining selections constrain response shapes in sulfur-containing carbonyls, a boronate, halogenated diesters, nitrile and halide ketones, aromatic esters and a large nonpolar aromatic scaffold. The fixed-loading sulfur-aldehyde and bromoterphenyl ratio pairs test predicted maxima rather than assuming monotonic curves. They provide useful counterexamples if broad corrections learned from polar compounds are spreading too far. Closely related selections are retained when they form a local experiment; identical recorded tuples are not duplicated within this batch.

With no pending experiments, these are all 32 acquisitions. The supplied forecasts remain frozen; rounded forecasts in reasons are explanatory only. Selection uses measured relationships and model behavior rather than treating quantile widths as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Elution interval width is not uncertainty. Missing experimental factors limit mechanistic interpretation, so the intended learning is about recorded structure–condition–endpoint relationships that may improve retrained accuracy across the Row-distribution.
